name: 1566 celestial phenomenon over Basel
description: A broadsheet published in 1566 depicted numerous spherical objects appearing out of the sun. Recorded by Samuel Coccius, a student of Holy Scripture and free arts at Basel.

name: Foo Fighters over Rhine Valley
description: Allied night-fighter pilots of the U.S. 415th Night Fighter Squadron reported small glowing orange balls of light following their aircraft over the Rhine Valley. The phenomenon, dubbed 'foo fighters' by the crews, was investigated by the Eighth Air Force and remained officially unexplained.

name: Scandinavian Ghost Rockets
description: Over 2,000 reports of rocket-shaped objects flying over Sweden, Finland and other Nordic countries were logged by civilian witnesses and military radar between May and December 1946. The Swedish military, with US and UK assistance, investigated and suspected Soviet tests of captured German V-weapons; roughly 200 reports remained unidentified after radar tracking.

name: Kenneth Arnold Mt. Rainier sighting
description: Private pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine high-speed crescent-shaped objects flying in formation near Mount Rainier. His description of their motion as 'like a saucer if you skip it across water' is credited with originating the term 'flying saucer' in the US press.

name: Roswell incident

location.name: Foster Ranch, near Corona, New Mexico, USA

description: Debris from a balloon-borne scientific instrument crashed on the Foster Ranch ~120km NW of Roswell. Initial Army Air Force press release said a 'flying disc' had been recovered, later retracted. AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report attributes the debris to Project MOGUL.
aaroMention: AARO Historical Record Report Vol. 1 (March 2024) attributes the debris to Project MOGUL balloon, finding no evidence of extraterrestrial origin or cover-up.

name: McMinnville UFO photographs (Trent farm)
description: Farmer Paul Trent took two photographs of a metallic disk-shaped object hovering above his farm near Sheridan, Oregon. The photos were published in Life magazine and analyzed by the USAF-funded Condon Committee, which classified the case as 'unexplained' on photographic grounds.

name: Mariana UFO film (Great Falls, Montana)
description: Local baseball team manager Nick Mariana filmed two bright silvery objects rotating across the sky above Legion Stadium — one of the earliest pieces of motion-picture footage of a UFO. The Air Force initially called the objects reflections of two F-94 jets, then retracted; Project Blue Book classified the film as unexplained.
imageLicense: Public domain (US gov, Project Blue Book)

name: Lubbock Lights
description: Texas Tech freshman Carl Hart Jr. photographed five frames of a V-shaped formation of bright lights flying over Lubbock. The photos were reprinted by Life magazine and analyzed by the Wright-Patterson AFB physics laboratory; Project Blue Book chief Edward Ruppelt later wrote the photos were never proven hoax nor genuine.

name: Captain Mantell crash
description: Kentucky Air National Guard pilot Captain Thomas Mantell died when his P-51 Mustang crashed while pursuing a large metallic object over Godman Air Force Base. Project Sign and later Blue Book concluded he had likely chased a Skyhook balloon and lost consciousness from hypoxia.

name: Washington D.C. radar flap
description: Multiple unidentified targets were tracked on radar at Washington National Airport and Andrews Air Force Base over two consecutive weekends, with corroborating visual sightings by airline and military pilots. The events triggered the largest Air Force press conference since WWII; Blue Book attributed them to temperature inversions, though Captain Edward Ruppelt and several controllers disputed that explanation.

name: Trindade Island photographs
description: Photographer Almiro Baraúna, aboard the Brazilian Navy ship Almirante Saldanha, captured four photographs of a Saturn-shaped object near Trindade Island. The negatives were examined by the Brazilian Navy and personally endorsed by President Juscelino Kubitschek, though later analyses by skeptics have suggested possible darkroom manipulation.

name: Betty and Barney Hill abduction
description: Betty and Barney Hill reported being followed by a luminous craft on US Route 3 in the White Mountains and later, under hypnosis, recalled an alleged abduction. The case became the first widely publicized abduction account in the US; the original notes are archived at the University of New Hampshire.

name: Michigan 'swamp gas' sightings
description: Dozens of witnesses including police officers and university students reported glowing objects over swampland near Dexter and Hillsdale, Michigan. Project Blue Book consultant J. Allen Hynek's tentative 'swamp gas' explanation drew public ridicule and contributed to congressional hearings led by Gerald Ford.

name: Falcon Lake incident (Stephen Michalak)
description: Geologist Stephen Michalak reported encountering a landed disc in Whiteshell Provincial Park and was burned by exhaust from a grid-patterned vent. The RCMP and RCAF investigated; contemporary newspaper photographs of the chest burns and Michalak's drawing of the craft survive. CBC has called it Canada's best-documented UFO case.
imageLicense: Fair use (Wikipedia, may break if status changes)

name: Shag Harbour incident
description: Multiple witnesses including RCMP officers reported a large illuminated object descending into the waters off Shag Harbour, prompting a search-and-rescue operation by the Royal Canadian Navy. Canadian government files released decades later confirmed the case was officially classified as a UFO of unknown origin.

name: Lake Cote UFO photograph (Costa Rica)
description: The Instituto Geográfico Nacional de Costa Rica was running an aerial mapping survey for the state electricity institute (ICE) when its government-owned camera captured a metallic disc over Lake Cote on a single frame (#300). Investigative journalist Leslie Kean has called it one of the strongest UFO photographs ever taken because it came from a controlled government mapping flight.
imageLicense: Use with attribution required: Instituto Geográfico Nacional de Costa Rica

name: Skylab 3 — unexplained object photographs

location.name: Low Earth Orbit (over SW Indian Ocean)

description: Skylab 3 crew photographed a reddish, rotating object during EVA over the southwestern Indian Ocean. PURSUE 2026 publishes the original NASA mission transcripts and unannotated frames.

name: Tehran F-4 incident
description: Two Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 Phantom jets were scrambled to intercept a brilliant unidentified object over Tehran and reportedly experienced instrumentation and weapons-system failures. The incident was documented in a US Defense Intelligence Agency report later released under FOIA and distributed to the White House, NSA and CIA.

name: Petrozavodsk phenomenon
description: Residents of Petrozavodsk in Soviet Karelia reported a luminous jellyfish-shaped object that hovered for several minutes and projected beams of light, with similar reports from Helsinki and Vladivostok. The Soviet Academy of Sciences opened the long-running 'Setka-AN' research program partly in response; the event was later linked to the launch of Kosmos-955 from Plesetsk.

name: Operação Prato (Colares)
description: Residents of Colares Island in the Amazon delta reported persistent encounters with luminous objects locally called 'chupa-chupa' that allegedly caused burns and puncture wounds. The Brazilian Air Force ran a covert investigation called Operação Prato; its files, photographs and reports were declassified in 2005.

name: Frederick Valentich disappearance
description: 20-year-old pilot Frederick Valentich vanished while flying a Cessna 182 over Bass Strait after radioing Melbourne ATC about a long metallic object 'orbiting' his aircraft. Neither Valentich nor the plane were ever found; the Australian Department of Transport's official accident report lists the cause as unknown.

name: Kaikoura lights
description: A Safe Air Argosy freighter crew flying along the east coast of New Zealand's South Island recorded unidentified lights tracked simultaneously by Wellington ATC radar; an Australian TV crew later filmed the lights on a follow-up flight. The Royal New Zealand Air Force investigated and could not conclusively identify the objects.

name: Manises (TAE 1284) incident
description: TAE Supercaravelle flight 1284 from Salzburg to Las Palmas was forced to make an emergency landing at Manises Airport in Valencia after the crew reported being paced by red lights. A Spanish Air Force Mirage F1 was scrambled and also detected the targets on radar; the incident was later officially declassified by the Spanish Ministry of Defence.

name: Rendlesham Forest incident
description: US Air Force personnel from RAF Bentwaters reported unexplained lights and a metallic craft in Rendlesham Forest over several nights. Often called 'Britain's Roswell'.

name: Trans-en-Provence case
description: Farmer Renato Nicolaï reported a disc-shaped object landing briefly in his garden in southern France, leaving circular ground traces. CNES's GEPAN unit collected soil and plant samples whose analysis by INRA showed biochemical anomalies, making it one of the most thoroughly documented physical-trace cases on file with a national space agency.

name: Hudson Valley sightings
description: Thousands of witnesses across New York's Hudson Valley and western Connecticut reported a large, slow-moving boomerang-shaped craft with multicolored lights between 1982 and 1986. The FAA and local police logged hundreds of calls; astronomer J. Allen Hynek documented the cases.

name: Japan Air Lines flight 1628 incident
description: A JAL 747 cargo flight reported being escorted by two small craft and a large 'mothership' over eastern Alaska near Fort Yukon. Picked up on both military and civilian radar.

name: Belgian UFO wave (triangle sightings)
description: Hundreds of witnesses, including police officers, reported a large, silent, triangular craft over Belgium between November 1989 and April 1990. Tracked on radar by the Belgian Air Force.

name: Calvine UFO photograph (Scotland)
description: Two hikers near the hamlet of Calvine photographed a large diamond-shaped craft hovering silently over the Perthshire moors with a Royal Air Force Harrier visible alongside. The negatives were handed to the Daily Record and forwarded to the UK Ministry of Defence, where they vanished for 32 years; one print resurfaced in 2022 and was the subject of a Sheffield Hallam University photographic analysis paper.

name: Ariel School encounter
description: Approximately 62 children at the Ariel School in Ruwa reported seeing a silver disc land near their playground during morning break and described seeing small humanoid figures. The case was investigated by Harvard psychiatrist John Mack and BBC journalist Tim Leach; notable for the consistency of children's drawings collected immediately after the event.

name: Varginha incident
description: Three young women in Varginha reported encountering a strange humanoid creature, with subsequent claims of military and fire-brigade recovery operations involving one or more entities. The Brazilian Air Force has officially denied any cover-up, but the case prompted a 2010 hearing and partial declassification of military files held by the Brazilian Aeronautics Command.

name: Phoenix Lights
description: Thousands of witnesses across Arizona, Nevada and Sonora reported a series of stationary and moving lights, including a triangular formation that passed over Phoenix.

name: USS Nimitz 'Tic Tac' encounter
description: F/A-18F pilots from Carrier Air Wing 11 operating with the USS Nimitz strike group encountered a fast-moving white oblong 'Tic Tac' shaped object off the coast of Baja California, with corroborating radar tracks from the USS Princeton. The DoD officially released the FLIR1 video in 2017; the incident is documented in the 2021 ODNI preliminary assessment on UAP.
aaroMention: AARO has reviewed the 2004 Nimitz encounter; the case is referenced in AARO's UAP case resolution materials and 2024 historical record context.

name: O'Hare International Airport sighting
description: United Airlines pilots, mechanics and ramp workers at Chicago O'Hare reported a metallic disc-shaped object hovering over Gate C-17 before reportedly punching a hole through the cloud layer as it departed. The FAA initially denied receiving reports but later released audio tapes under FOIA; officially classified as a 'weather phenomenon.'

name: USS Theodore Roosevelt — GIMBAL encounter
description: Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet captured FLIR footage of a rotating, wingless object travelling against high-altitude winds. Released by DoD; reaffirmed and contextualized in the May 2026 PURSUE drop.
aaroMention: GIMBAL is one of the three official Navy UAP videos acknowledged by DoD (April 2020); referenced across AARO public materials and the FY2022/FY2023 ODNI/AARO consolidated UAP reports.

name: GOFAST encounter
description: Companion FLIR footage to GIMBAL showing a small object skimming low over the ocean at high speed. PURSUE 2026 release includes the original mission debrief.
aaroMention: GO FAST is one of the three official Navy UAP videos acknowledged by DoD (April 2020); cited in AARO public communications and ODNI/AARO consolidated annual UAP reports.

name: Western US — orbs launching orbs
description: Federal law enforcement officers independently reported strange incidents involving orbs across two days, including 'orbs launching other orbs'. The Pentagon describes this as 'among the most compelling' of the holdings released in PURSUE.
aaroMention: Pentagon/AARO May 2026 release (DOW-UAP-PR47, 'Western US Event 2023') describes federal law-enforcement reports of orange orbs emitting smaller red orbs over the western US in 2023. Characterized by DoD as 'among the most compelling within AARO's current holdings.'
